senses: Connected with weeping or tears.
ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin lachrymālis, from lachryma (“a tear”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix). Doublet of lacrimal.

senses: A low, horizontal cloud typically forming at the leading edge of thunderstorm outflow
ety: Borrowed from Latin arcus. Doublet of arc and arco. Distantly related to arrow.

senses: To lay aside; to stop; to cancel.
ety: From Middle English beleggen, bileggen, from Old English beleċġan (“to cover, invest, surround, afflict, attribute to, charge with, accuse”), From Proto-West Germanic *bilaggjan, equivalent to be- (“about, around”) + lay. Cognate with Dutch beleggen (“to cover, overlay, belay”), German belegen (“to cover, occupy, belay”), Swedish belägga (“to pave”).

senses: The process of sonifying.
examples: In another project, Weather sonification (Flowers and al., 2001), the correlation is made between different types of data, such as air pressure and temperature, with musical instruments.
Sonification is a subset of a larger field called Auditory Display, which examines how sound can be used as the main conduit for conveying, understanding, and relaying information.
Over the past 20 years, there have been many explorations and examples of sonifications.

senses: brother-in-law
A valve used to turn something off.
The act of turning something off.
examples: The fire raged for hours because they were unable to reach the shutoff for the gas line.
The letter warned of an impending shutoff if payment was not made promptly.

senses: Articles made from brass, treated as a group.
A surplice, in England and America usually one shorter and less full than the ordinary surplice and with short sleeves, or sometimes none.
A kind of coarse woolen blanket.
examples: She wore a short surcoat of scarlet, cut low around the shoulders, sleeveless, reaching just below her hips, like the tabards worn by medieval heralds. Over it she wore a laced-edged cotta.

senses: Homophonic; sounding the same.
ety: Adapted borrowing of Ancient Greek ὁμόφωνος (homóphōnos) + -ous. By surface analysis, homo- + -phonous.

senses: A governing body in certain universities.
A religious devotee or dervish in Persia.
ety: From Arabic أَبْدَال (ʔabdāl), plural of بَدَل (badal, “a substitute; a good, religious man; saint”), from بَدَلَ (badala, “to replace”).

senses: Such an alga or fungus
A form of jewel case for holding one or more CDs or DVDs, having an outer cover made of card rather than plastic.
ety: From the trademark Digipak, presumably from digi- + pack.

senses: Synonym of chocolaty.
examples: The house soon filled with a wonderful chocolately smell.

senses: A momentary vertical jet or fountain of fluid driven upwards by a violent force.
A domestic water boiler.
ety: From Icelandic Geysir (“Gusher”), the Icelandic name of a particular hot spring in Iceland (see Wikipedia), from the verb geysa (“to gush”), from Old Norse geysa (“to gush”), which is mentioned in English as early as the 1760s in The Annual Register, as “Geyser, a wonderful spring in the valley of Haukadal”. Doublet of gusher

senses: A French countess.
examples: The king is impatient to see the comtesse, and I have promised that she will sup with him to-morrow evening in my apartment at Versailles.

senses: An Arabic literary form, 'usually defined as an erotic or amatory prelude to the type of long poem called a qaṣīdah.'
A toasted flake of maize used as breakfast cereal.
In the manner of a pugilist.
Fighting with the fists.
examples: It was no time for pugilistic chivalry, and my brother laid him quiet with a kick, and gripped the collar of the man who pulled at the slender lady's arm.
Mr. Christie, who as a presidential candidate has frequently suppressed his most pugilistic instincts, cast off any restraint and did what he does best: slice and slash.

senses: A clear brandy made from black cherries: kirschwasser.
ety: Borrowed from French kirsch, from German Kirschwasser (“cherry water”). Doublet of cerise and cherry.

senses: Finicky; overly critical; concerned with insignificant details.
Semiotics, the study of signs.
The art of using signs in signalling.
The symptom expression of an epileptic seizure.
ety: From New Latin semaeologia, from Ancient Greek σημεῖον (sēmeîon, “sign”) + -logia (“-logy”). By surface analysis, semio- + -logy.

senses: A sailor, especially one in the Royal Navy.
ety: A borrowing from Middle French nautique (“of or relating to sailors or navigation”) and a learned borrowing from its etymon, Classical Latin nauticus (“of or relating to ships, seafaring”), from Ancient Greek ναυτικός (nautikós), from ναύτης (naútēs, “sailor”) + -ικός (-ikós, adjectival suffix). Compare earlier nautical (likewise also used as a noun; compare Classical Latin nauticus (“sailor”)).
examples: A complete reversal of policy was now thrust upon an eager company of flying nautics.

senses: One who collects bees into a hive.
A peasant who performed labour in exchange for the right to live in a cottage.
ety: From Middle English cotter, cotere, kottere, koter, cotier, equivalent to cot (“cottage”) + -er, from Old English cot. Compare Old French coter, cotier.

senses: A person who migrated to Pakistan after the Partition of India in August 1947, or one of the descendants.
ety: Borrowed from Arabic مُهَاجِر (muhājir, literally “emigrant”). Sense 2 is from its Urdu derivative مُہَاجِر (muhājir).

senses: the branch of geophysics that studies the deformation processes of planetary mantle and crust, and the resulting earthquakes and volcanism
Calm, collected and unconfused; not nonplussed (“bewildered, unsure how to react”).
Bothered, fazed, vexed, or concerned; not nonplussed (“unfazed, unaffected, unimpressed”).
ety: A back-formation from nonplussed; see that entry for more on its own sense development.
examples: Jady was rarely nonplussed, normally being very plussed indeed, but Alison's ability to move events without really noticing astounded him. She ran her hair idly through her fingers.

senses: Someone who performs in vaudeville.
examples: Harris was born in Richmond, Virginia, on February 9, 1947. His grandparents were vaudevillians, his father was a professional guitarist, and his mother was a leader of the church choir.

senses: Someone who rides a motorcycle.
A small or miniature shell.
examples: As you would expect, the first shelled organisms acquired a shell in small steps, forming tiny (less than 1 mm) hard parts nicknamed "little shellies" or "small shellies."

senses: Synonym of dream yoga.
Having none of a particular kind of adhesion on the outside of its lungs; only meat from a glatt animal can be kosher.
Having no ingredients from animals that are not glatt.
ety: Borrowed from Yiddish גלאַט (glat, “smooth”). Doublet of glad.

senses: Ready to dance.
Of music: suitable for dancing to.
examples: I'm feeling a bit dancy today.
Gear up for a bit of a walk—five whole minutes to The George on S. George St. We're all loosened up and ready to get a little dancey at this thoroughly festive gay club.
After a few slow numbers, the band moved on to some more dancy tunes.

senses: Radio channel based data connection.
A way of traveling between two places in planes or helicopters.
examples: The gateway also allows the carrier to support multiple airlink standards including CDMA, CDPD, GSM, iDEN, PDC, PHS, and TDMA.
I am very grateful for this opportunity to debate the Heathrow to Gatwick helicopter airlink.

senses: Not allowable
For which an allowance may not be claimed
A Southeast Asian tree (Lagerstroemia speciosa), with medicinal leaves.
ety: Ultimately from Proto-Philippine *banabá. Compare Tagalog banabá, Cebuano banaba, Kapampangan [Term?].

senses: To make (into) sauerkraut.
ety: Clipping of sauerkraut, from German Sauerkraut. Compare German Kraut (“cabbage”).
examples: They krauted cabbage, picked saskatoons and dried them for the winter. The whole family contributed to the welfare of the home for there was no room for a drone in their midst.

senses: Any of many thick Italian vegetable soups.
ety: Directly from Italian minestrone, from minestra (“soup”, ultimately from Latin ministrō) + -one (augmentative suffix).

senses: Someone who reforges.
